lines.text: Here's how Claude Code runs in the cloud, in under sixty seconds.
Say your app has a test that fails at random, out-of-date docs, and a logger that should print JSON. You hand each job to Claude in the cloud.
Each task gets a fresh virtual machine, with your repository cloned onto a new branch, so push your commits first.
Your GitHub token never enters that machine. A proxy holds it and gives the session a short-lived credential that can push only to its own branch.
Because every task has its own machine, all three run at once. In one experiment, all three finished within eighty-seven seconds of the first one starting.
The sessions can't see each other, so split the work along file boundaries.
Each job comes back as a branch you can turn into a pull request.
For a local database, a V P N only service, or a G P U, stay on your laptop.
